# Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

## Goal

Run the committed pipeline over the gathered footage to produce and validate
the actual deliverables and manifests: the ~45–60 s promo, the > 2 min
showreel, and several short highlight clips — all 960×540 WebM with the game's
SFX — accompanied by the selection and coverage manifests, and verify the
attention-grabbing pace criteria (AC1–AC4 of the parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can share a compelling promo package that
opens with action and showcases weapons, pickups and enemies.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables produced.** `capture-output/` contains: the compiled
  promo WebM (~45–60 s), the showreel WebM (> 2 min), and several highlight
  clips — all at 960×540 with an audio track (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback).
- **AC2 — Manifests produced.** The selection manifest (source WebM, series,
  mapped timestamps, motivating intensities) and the coverage manifest
  (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) accompany the deliverables; all three
  feature categories (weapons, pickups, enemies; boss when available) are
  listed.
- **AC3 — Pace verified.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the
  first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks; verification measures the sampled non-black
  frame ratio and the average recorded intensity, and confirms they are at or
  above the documented reference band. The **reference band is documented**
  as part of this item (with the calibration basis).
- **AC4 — Per-clip intensities reported.** The manifest prints the per-clip
  recorded intensities so the pace claim is auditable.
- **AC5 — Validated.** Each deliverable passes the pipeline's validation step
  (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

- **Covers parent AC1:** **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.

## Key files

- `capture-output/` — gitignored deliverables + manifests
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — the pipeline under test at runtime
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — reference band documented here

## Implementation notes

- This is a run/verify item: the *code* is delivered by the earlier items; this
  item executes the pipeline and records the evidence (file paths, durations,
  resolution, audio verdict, non-black ratio, mean intensity).
- If footage cannot evidence a category or the pace band is not met, record the
  gap explicitly and create a follow-up item rather than weakening the ACs.

## Deliverables

- The promo, showreel and highlight clips + both manifests + a pace report
  (comment on this item).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the ffmpeg driver (C5) and the gathered footage (C6).

# Unit/integration Vitest project split

**Goal:** Split the single Vitest project into two: a fast `unit` project
(`environment: 'node'`, non-Phaser test files — roughly 174 of 270) for the TDD
loop, and an `integration` project (happy-dom + Phaser + current
`src/test/setup.ts`) for the heavy suite. The full run still executes both so
`/skill:test --type full` keeps its audit contract, while `--type unit` becomes
a sub-minute fast feedback loop (parent AC2, AC6, AC7).

**Deliverables**

- `vitest.config.ts` with a `projects` array: `unit` (node environment, no
  `deps.inline: ['phaser']`, no DOM setup) and `integration` (happy-dom,
  `setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts']`, `deps.inline: ['phaser']`).
- A deterministic, documented selection rule for "non-Phaser": the parent
  assumes static separability, but a file may import `phaser` transitively via
  `src/scenes/**`. Pick and document one rule (e.g. an explicit integration
  include list plus unit = remainder, or a generated classification) and record
  the file/test counts per project.
- A project-membership test asserting every `*.test.ts` under `src/`, `scripts/`
  and `vite/` is selected by exactly one project (no orphan, no duplicate), so
  an unclassifiable new file fails loudly (parent AC7).
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` registering
  `{"types": {"unit": ["npx vitest run --project unit"]}}` — the producer
  explicitly approved this `.pi/` edit during intake (2026-10-19, see parent
  Appendix). `--type full` must still fall back to the full suite.
- `package.json`: a `test:unit` script (keep `npm --silent test` as the
  full-suite entry point); coverage config preserved (or attached to the project
  that owns the covered modules) so `test:coverage` thresholds do not regress.

**Key Files:**

- `./vitest.config.ts` — projects, per-project environment/include/deps
- `src/test/setup.ts` — integration-only; no-op/excluded for unit
- `./package.json` — `test`, `test:unit`, `test:coverage`
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — new, producer-approved
- `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` (new project-membership test)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `npx vitest run --project unit` selects only non-Phaser test files
  and completes in ≤ 60 s on an idle 16-core host, with the measured command,
  the selection rule, and the per-project file/test counts recorded on this item
  and the parent.
- **AC2:** The `integration` project selects all Phaser/DOM-booting test files
  and passes standalone (`npx vitest run --project integration`).
- **AC3:** A project-membership test asserts every test file is selected by
  exactly one project and fails if a file belongs to none or to both (parent
  AC7).
- **AC4:** `/skill:test --type full` still executes both projects and remains
  the audit-accepted full-suite evidence (`scope: full`, `test_type: full`,
  `exit_code: 0`); `/skill:test --type unit` runs via the extension and uses an
  independent cache key that can never satisfy a full-suite AC (parent AC6).
- **AC5:** `npm run test:coverage` still enforces the existing per-file line
  thresholds (no coverage regression), and `npm --silent test` remains the
  full-suite entry point (parent constraint).
- **AC6:** No test deleted, skipped or re-classified to make a project pass;
  any file that cannot be classified is reported as an Open Question rather than
  silently dropped.
- **AC7:** Testing/validation — new and changed behaviour is covered by tests:
  the project-membership test above (every test file selected by exactly one
  project, no orphaned or duplicated file), the deterministic-boot guard test
  from the harness sibling item (AH-0MVF6XQIC005RY3P), and the timing
  measurements from AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ re-runnable from a documented command.

**Constraints:** `.pi/` editing is limited strictly to the approved extension
file. Audit gate compatibility (`implement.py finish`, pre-push hook, audit F3
cache lookup) must be preserved.

**References:** Parent AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV § Desired change 3, AC2, AC6, AC7,
Constraints; test skill § 1a typed runs (extension contract).

data.description:
## Problem

The Node capture-side series exporter (`extractActionIntensitySeriesFromRecords` in `scripts/capture-series.mjs`) assigns each retained sample `t = samples.length * gridMs` (100 ms at 10 Hz) instead of deriving time from the telemetry record. Consecutive samples whose metric values are identical are collapsed, so the exported `t` axis compresses whenever the metric is unchanged between grid steps.

Evidence from the C6 capture pool (AH-0MVDV4SYG008X8TY):

- Run `gameplay-2026-10-19T16-51-02-526Z`: capture reports `runLengthMs: 110457` and the series' last record carries `tick: 739`.
- Exported series `gameplay-2026-10-19T16-51-02-526Z.action.jsonl`: 440 samples, last sample `t = 43900` — i.e. the timeline claims 43.9 s although the run was ~110 s.
- Boss runs show the same pattern (e.g. 54.9 s clip, 90 samples, series horizon 8.9 s).

Impact: §7.5 video-join maps a series time to video time via `videoTimeMs(t) = t − offsetMs`. A compressed `t` axis therefore maps selected peaks to the wrong video position. The promo compiler's selection manifest (parent AC2, C7 AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4) claims "mapped video timestamps" for each pick, so this undermines the verifiability requirement.

## Expected behaviour

- The exported series `t` must represent real time since run start (within the documented sample grid) for every retained sample, even when consecutive metric values are identical.
- Either derive `t` from the telemetry record's own clock/tick (with a documented tick→ms conversion) or emit a sample per grid step instead of collapsing the timeline.
- Update `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.2/§7.5 if the contract changes, and add a regression test with a run longer than the collapsed sample count.

## References

- `scripts/capture-series.mjs` — `extractActionIntensitySeriesFromRecords`
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` — `t` contract ("milliseconds since run start")
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.2–§7.5
- Discovered while gathering footage: AH-0MVDV4SYG008X8TY
- Blocks accurate selection manifests: AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4
